'''Goga Bitadze''' (born 20 July 1999) is a Georgian professional [[basketball]] player for [[KK Mega Basket|Mega Bemax]] of the [[ABA League]], and the [[Basketball League of Serbia|Serbian League]]. Listed at {{height|m=2.12}} and 114 kilograms (251 lbs), he plays the [[center (basketball)|center]] position.<ref name="eurospects">{{cite web |title=Goga Bitadze |url=https://eurospects.com/?page_id=1171 |publisher=Eurospects |accessdate=6 February 2019}}</ref> He is considered one of the top international prospects and a potential first-round pick in the [[2019 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kalbrosky |first1=Bryan |title=2019 aggregate NBA mock draft 4.0: Murray State's Ja Morant is Top 3 |url=https://hoopshype.com/2019/01/22/nba-mock-draft-big-board-rumor-update-prospects/ |publisher=HoopsHype |accessdate=6 February 2019 |date=22 January 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Woo |first1=Jeremy |title=2019 NBA Mock Draft 3.0: Zion Williamson Remains on Top, Ja Morant Continues to Skyrocket |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2019/01/30/nba-mock-draft-2019-zion-williamson-rj-barrett-ja-morant-cam-reddish |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |accessdate=6 February 2019 |date=30 January 2019}}</ref>

Born in [[Sagarejo]], Bitadze started playing basketball professionally with [[B.C. VITA Tbilisi|VITA Tbilisi]] in the [[VTB United League]]. In 2015, he moved to Serbian club Mega Basket and was loaned to [[Basketball League of Serbia|Serbian League]] team [[KK Smederevo 1953|Smederevo 1953]] in the following year. Upon his return to Mega in 2017–18, Bitadze was named [[most valuable player]] (MVP) of the [[Junior ABA League]] and became a key player for the senior team. At the end of 2018, he was loaned to [[KK Budućnost|Budućnost]] in Montenegro and was named [[EuroLeague Rising Star]] for the 2018–19 season.

Bitadze is a member of the [[Georgia men's national basketball team|Georgian national basketball team]]. He was named to the national team at [[EuroBasket 2017]] and made his debut at [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Europe)|FIBA World Cup qualifiers]] in 2017. Previously, Bitadze represented Georgia at the junior level in [[FIBA]] competition.

== Early life and career ==
Bitadze was born in [[Sagarejo]], a town in eastern [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]].<ref name="hein">{{cite web |last1=Hein |first1=David |title=Bitadze goes from land of wrestlers to talent-developing Mega |url=http://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/7rc5kkcryt8dtc4f/bitadze-goes-from-land-of-wrestlers-to-talent-developing-mega |publisher=[[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] |accessdate=30 January 2019 |date=21 April 2017}}</ref> His father was a professional basketball player whose career was cut short by injury.<ref name="interview">{{cite web |last1=Simonishvili |first1=Vazha |title=NBA-ის კემპი, იოკიჩი, ფაჩულია - ინტერვიუ გოგა ბითაძესთან |url=https://sportall.ge/kalatburti/qarthuli-kalathburthi/legionerebi/105511-nba-is-kempi-iokichi-fachulia-interviu-goga-bithadzesthan.html |publisher=SportAll |accessdate=30 January 2019 |language=Georgian |date=25 June 2017}}</ref> Although Bitadze did not watch basketball in his childhood, he started playing the game when he was 6 years old, because he saw himself as "active and tall."<ref name=hein/> As he became more involved in basketball, he began idolizing Georgian players [[Zaza Pachulia]] and [[Tornike Shengelia]], as well as NBA stars [[Pau Gasol]] and [[Shaquille O'Neal]].<ref name=hein/><ref name=youtube>{{cite AV media|people=Bitadze, Goga, and Jonathan Givony|date=12 September 2016|title=Goga Bitadze Interview from NBA Basketball Without Borders Europe Camp|medium=Video|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kZrf8aEjZfY|location=[[Finland]]|publisher=DraftExpress}}</ref> On 31 May 2013, Bitadze scored 17 points to help his school team [[Hyundai Motor Company|Hyundai]] win the national under-14 championship over Gori.<ref>{{cite web |title=1-ელი ექსპერიმენტალური სკოლის გუნდი "ჰიუნდაი" ჩემპიონია! |url=http://gbf.ge/league/u14/news/1-eli-eqsperimentaluri-skolis-gundi-hiundai-chempionia |publisher=[[Georgian Basketball Federation]] |accessdate=30 January 2019 |language=Georgian |date=31 May 2013}}</ref> He also played in the Georgian under-16 league for three years. In 2014–15, his final season with Hyundai at the under-16 level, Bitadze averaged 23.1 points, 16.6 rebounds, 4.5 assists, and 3.8 blocks per game.<ref name="u16">{{cite web |title=Goga Bitadze |url=http://gbf.ge/en/league/u16/player/5552711 |publisher=[[Georgian Basketball Federation]] |accessdate=30 January 2019}}</ref> Through his early career, Bitadze trained in the junior ranks of Georgian club [[B.C. VITA Tbilisi|VITA Tbilisi]].<ref name="fernandez">{{cite web |last1=Fernández |first1=Marcos |title=Conoce al pívot georgiano Goga Bitadze: la sensación del Adidas Next Generation |url=https://www.gigantes.com/cantera/competiciones-torneos-y-campeonatos/conoce-al-pivot-georgiano-goga-bitadze-la-sensacion-del-adidas-next-generation-video/ |publisher=Gigantes del Basket |accessdate=30 January 2019 |language=Spanish |date=22 May 2017}}</ref>

== Professional career ==
=== VITA Tbilisi (2015–2016) ===
In the 2015–16 season, Bitadze played professionally for VITA Tbilisi in the [[VTB United League]].<ref name="realgm">{{cite web |title=Goga Bitadze Player Profile |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Goga-Bitadze/Summary/75906 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=31 January 2019}}</ref> He made his debut at age 16 and consequently became the youngest player in league history.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kharazov |first1=Levan |title=გოგა ბითაძე სერბულ "მეგა ლეკსში" გადავიდა |url=https://www.mysports.ge/ka/post/view/2132 |publisher=MySports |accessdate=31 January 2019 |language=Georgian |date=2 December 2015}}</ref> Through 6 games, Bitadze averaged 2.8 points, 1.7 rebounds, and 0.7 blocks in 13.8 minutes per game.<ref name="vtb">{{cite web |title=Goga Bitadze |url=http://old.vtb-league.com/en/player/goga-bitadze.htm |publisher=[[VTB United League]] |accessdate=31 January 2019}}</ref>

=== Mega Basket (2016–present) ===
==== Junior success and Smederevo loan (2016–17) ====
On 2 December 2015, he signed with [[KK Mega Basket|Mega Basket]] of the [[Basketball League of Serbia]] (KLS) and [[ABA League]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Obradovic |first1=Igor |title=Goga Bitadze (ex Vita Tbilisi) joins Mega Leks |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Serbia/news/429985/Former-players:-Goga-Bitadze-(ex-Vita-Tbilisi)-joins-Mega-Leks |publisher=[[Eurobasket.com|Eurobasket]] |accessdate=31 January 2019 |date=2 December 2015}}</ref> Bitadze was drawn to the club because it had produced many NBA players like [[Nikola Jokić]] and [[Ivica Zubac]], and he thought the Serbian league was "well run."<ref name=hein/><ref name="rangelov">{{cite web |last1=Rangelov |first1=Miloš |title=Ko je Goga Bitadze? Gruzijac od kojeg Mega pravi novog Jokića |url=https://sport.blic.rs/kosarka/domaca-kosarka-i-aba/cudo-od-deteta-ko-je-goga-bitadze-gruzijac-od-kojeg-mega-pravi-novog-jokica/j4h58te |website=[[Blic]] |accessdate=1 February 2019 |language=Serbian |date=21 May 2017}}</ref> He described the move, "It was hard for me for a couple of months. I was really frustrated, far away from my family and far away from my friends. It was hard, but then slowly I got used to it... you have to sacrifice in order to achieve something big and get something even bigger."<ref name="petrinovic">{{cite web |last1=Petrinovic |first1=Igor |title=Goga Bitadze, Buducnost: 'We are not going to give up' |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/interviews/euroleague-2018-19/i/9ecubovhtrpe8eu6/goga-bitadze-buducnost-we-are-not-going-to-give-up |publisher=[[EuroLeague]] |accessdate=31 January 2019 |date=15 January 2019}}</ref> In December 2015, Bitadze averaged 7.8 points and 4 rebounds per game to help Mega's junior team win the [[2015–16 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|Torneo Città di Roma]] and qualify for the [[2015–16 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|2015–16 Adidas Next Generation Tournament]] (ANGT).<ref name=realgm/><ref>{{cite web |title=Final, Stellazzurra Basketball vs. Mega Leks Belgrade - Torneo Citta di Roma |url=http://admin.euroleague.net/u18/photos/2015-16/i/6ks6smaegigrphc4/final-stellazzurra-basketball-vs-mega-leks-belgrade-torneo-citta-di-roma |publisher=[[EuroLeague]] |accessdate=31 January 2019}}</ref> In three games at the ANGT, he averaged 4.7 points and 5.3 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bitadze, Goga |url=http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=006809&seasoncode=JTR15 |publisher=[[EuroLeague]] |accessdate=31 January 2019}}</ref>

For the 2016–17 season, Bitadze was [[Loan (sports)|loaned]] to Serbian club [[KK Smederevo 1953|Smederevo 1953]], which competed in the KLS.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |last2=Kamalsky |first2=Matt |title=2017 Adidas EuroCamp Rosters and Preview |url=http://www.draftexpress.com/article/2017-adidas-eurocamp-rosters-and-preview-5987/ |publisher=DraftExpress |accessdate=31 January 2019 |date=7 June 2017}}</ref> Through 19 games, he averaged 10.6 points, 4.4 rebounds, and 1.2 blocks per game.<ref name=realgm/> Bitadze debuted on October 8, 2016, recording 5 points and 4 rebounds in a 75–71 loss to [[KK Borac Čačak|Borac Čačak]].<ref>{{cite web |title=KK Smederevo 1953 71,  KK Borac Cacak 75 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2016-10-08/KK-Smederevo-1953-at-KK-Borac-Cacak/253992 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=31 January 2019 |date=8 October 2016}}</ref> On October 29 versus [[KK Napredak Kruševac|Napredak Kruševac]], he scored a season-high 18 points, a mark he would match three more times in the season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Goga Bitadze Game Logs |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Goga-Bitadze/GameLogs/75906/International/2017/13 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=31 January 2019}}</ref> Bitadze recorded his first [[double (basketball)|double-double]] on April 1, 2017 against [[KK Dunav Stari Banovci|Dunav Stari Banovci]], with 18 points and 11 rebounds.<ref>{{cite web |title=KK Smederevo 1953 86, KK Dunav Stari Banovci 75 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2017-04-01/KK-Smederevo-1953-at-KK-Dunav-Stari-Banovci/262976 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=31 January 2019 |date=1 April 2017}}</ref> In addition, he assumed a leading role for the Mega Basket junior team at the [[2016–17 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|2016–17 ANGT]]. Bitadze averaged 17.7 points per game and led the tournament with 10 rebounds and 3.8 blocks per contest, en route to making the All-Tournament Team.<ref>{{cite web |title=ANGT MVP Fevrier of Paris headlines All-Tournament Team |url=http://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/7tq4fg39g34kcdfy/angt-mvp-fevrier-of-paris-headlines-all-tournament-team |publisher=[[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] |accessdate=31 January 2019 |date=21 May 2017}}</ref>

==== Rise to stardom (2017–2018) ====
He returned to Mega entering the 2017–18 season and mainly played with the senior team.<ref name=realgm/> Through 22 games in the ABA League, Bitadze averaged 11.8 points, 6.2 rebounds, and 2.1 blocks per game, and through 12 games in the KLS, he averaged 15.9 points and 6.7 rebounds per game.<ref name="eurobasket">{{cite web |title=Goga Bitadze Basketball Player Profile |url=https://basketball.eurobasket.com/player/Goga_Bitadze/KK_Buducnost_Voli_Podgorica/369053 |publisher=[[Eurobasket.com|Eurobasket]] |accessdate=1 February 2019}}</ref> He debuted on 1 October 2017, recording 12 points, 9 rebounds, and 5 blocks in a 95–88 win over [[KK Cibona|Cibona]].<ref>{{cite web |title=KK Cibona 88, KK Mega Bemax 95 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2017-10-01/KK-Cibona-at-KK-Mega-Bemax/270477 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=1 February 2019 |date=1 October 2017}}</ref> In January 2018, Bitadze briefly played for Mega's junior team and helped capture the [[Junior ABA League]] championship. After averaging 17 points and 11 rebounds in the final tournament, he was named league MVP and earned Ideal Five recognition.<ref name="mvp">{{cite web |title=The MVP award belongs to Goga Bitadze |url=https://www.aba-liga.com/news.php?id=39766 |publisher=[[ABA League]] |accessdate=1 February 2019 |date=28 January 2018}}</ref> On 20 January, Bitadze scored 23 points versus [[KK Cedevita|Cedevita]], his season-high mark in the ABA League.<ref>{{cite web |title=KK Mega Bemax 73, Cedevita 75 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2018-01-20/KK-Mega-Bemax-at-Cedevita/290471 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=3 February 2019 |date=20 January 2018}}</ref> He declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]] on 12 April and was considered a possible second-round pick.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Georgian center Goga Bitadze declaring for NBA draft |url=http://www.espn.com/blog/nba/post/_/id/32639/georgian-center-goga-bitadze-declaring-for-nba-draft |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=6 February 2019 |date=12 April 2018}}</ref> Bitadze recorded 19 points and season-bests of 15 rebounds and 6 blocks on 24 April, in a 92–90 loss to [[KK Mladost Zemun|Mladost Zemun]] in the KLS.<ref>{{cite web |title=KK Mladost Admiral Zemun 92, KK Mega Bemax 90 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2018-04-24/KK-Mladost-Admiral-Zemun-at-KK-Mega-Bemax/304480 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=3 February 2019 |date=24 April 2018}}</ref> On 30 May, he had his best scoring effort of the season, posting 25 points on 9-of-12 shooting in an 83–61 victory over [[KK Vršac|Vršac]] in KLS play.<ref>{{cite web |title=KK Mega Bemax 83, KK Vrsac Swisslion 61 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2018-05-30/KK-Mega-Bemax-at-KK-Vrsac-Swisslion/306906 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=3 February 2019 |date=30 May 2018}}</ref> Bitadze withdrew from the 2018 NBA draft on 11 June, less than two weeks from draft night.<ref>{{cite web |title=Charalampopoulos, Bitadze withdraw from 2018 NBA draft |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/692834/charalampopoulos-bitadze-withdraw-from-2018-nba-draft/ |publisher=EuroHoops |accessdate=6 February 2019 |date=11 June 2018}}</ref>

To start the 2018–19 season, he continued playing for Mega. In an exhibition game versus [[NCAA Division I]] team [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] on 11 August 2018, Bitadze suffered an injury towards the end of the first half and did not return.<ref name="kentucky">{{cite web |title=Kentucky Convincing Against Mega, Milojevic: "Big Experience For Our Young Team" |url=http://www.bcmegabasket.net/en/2018/08/12/mega-bemax-kentaki-izvestaj/ |publisher=[[KK Mega Basket|Mega Basket]] |accessdate=4 February 2019 |date=12 August 2018}}</ref> On 30 September, in his ABA League season debut, he chipped in 24 points and 12 rebounds in an 80–79 win over [[KK Igokea|Igokea]].<ref>{{cite web |title=KK Mega Bemax 80, BC Igokea 79 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2018-09-30/KK-Mega-Bemax-at-BC-Igokea/308556 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=4 February 2019 |date=30 September 2018}}</ref> On 30 October, two days after recording 26 points, 10 rebounds, and 3 blocks against [[KK Mornar Bar|Mornar Bar]], Bitadze was named monthly MVP in the ABA League.<ref>{{cite web |title=MVP of October: Goga Bitadze (Mega Bemax) |url=https://www.aba-liga.com/news.php?id=40845 |publisher=[[ABA League]] |accessdate=4 February 2019 |date=30 October 2018}}</ref> In his following appearance on 3 November, he scored a season-high 28 points, shooting 10-of-11 from the field, while posting 11 rebounds and 4 blocks in an 81–74 loss to [[KK Partizan|Partizan]].<ref>{{cite web |title=KK Partizan 81, KK Mega Bemax 74 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2018-11-03/KK-Partizan-at-KK-Mega-Bemax/322348 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=4 February 2019 |date=3 November 2018}}</ref> On 24 November, Bitadze scored 28 points again, leading his team to an 82–80 victory over Cibona.<ref>{{cite web |title=KK Cibona 80, KK Mega Bemax 82 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2018-11-24/KK-Cibona-at-KK-Mega-Bemax/322423 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=4 February 2019 |date=24 November 2018}}</ref> Through 11 games for Mega, all of which were in the ABA League, he averaged 20.2 points, 7.9 rebounds, and 2.6 blocks per game.<ref name=realgm/>

=== Budućnost (2018–2019) ===
On 20 December 2018, Bitadze was loaned to Montenegrin club [[KK Budućnost|Budućnost]], which competed in the [[Prva A Liga|Montenegrin League]], ABA League, and [[EuroLeague]].<ref name="buducnost">{{cite web |title=Buducnost adds young star Bitadze |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/9ca7iicfwhxyspfa/buducnost-adds-young-star-bitadze |publisher=[[EuroLeague]] |accessdate=4 February 2019 |date=20 December 2018}}</ref> He joined the team for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bitadze on loan in Buducnost until the end of ABA League |url=http://www.bcmegabasket.net/en/2018/12/20/bitadze-na-pozajmici-u-buducnosti-do-kraja-aba-lige/ |publisher=[[KK Mega Basket|Mega Basket]] |accessdate=5 February 2019 |date=20 December 2018}}</ref> Reflecting on the transition to his new club, Bitadze said, "It was not an easy situation, especially the first couple of days. I mean, it is still hard now to get used to things. But my teammates and coaches helped me."<ref name=petrinovic/> In his first game for Budućnost, on 24 December, he recorded 12 points and 4 rebounds versus [[KK Krka|Krka]] in the ABA League.<ref>{{cite web |title=Buducnost 64, Krka Novo Mesto 69 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2018-12-24/Buducnost-at-Krka-Novo-Mesto/322567 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=5 February 2019 |date=24 December 2018}}</ref> Four days later, Bitadze made his EuroLeague debut, chipping in 17 points, 7 rebounds, and 4 blocks in a 93–88 loss to [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Bayern rallies from 17 down, overcomes Buducnost |url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=119&seasoncode=E2018#!report |publisher=[[EuroLeague]] |accessdate=5 February 2019 |date=28 December 2018}}</ref> On 3 January 2019, he had another strong EuroLeague performance, posting 23 points, 8 rebounds, and 3 blocks off the bench in a 111–94 defeat to [[Pallacanestro Olimpia Milano|Olimpia Milano]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Milan blasts Buducnost with record scoring performance |url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=122&seasoncode=E2018#!report |publisher=[[EuroLeague]] |accessdate=5 February 2019 |date=3 January 2019}}</ref> After 13 games, Bitadze averaged 12.1 points, 6.4 rebounds and 2.3 blocks per game and claimed [[EuroLeague Rising Star]] honors as the best under-22 player in the EuroLeague.<ref name="risingstar">{{cite web |title=Goga Bitadze named EuroLeague Rising Star |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/873787/goga-bitadze-named-euroleague-rising-star/ |publisher=EuroHoops |accessdate=16 May 2019 |date=7 May 2019}}</ref>

== National team career ==
=== Junior national team ===
Bitadze played for the [[Georgia national under-17 basketball team|Georgian national under-17 team]] at the 2015 [[FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]] Division B, averaging 14.2 points, 8.8 rebounds, and 3.7 blocks per game en route to a fifth-place finish.<ref name=realgm/> He had his best scoring display in the tournament on 13 August 2015, posting 24 points and 11 rebounds in an 80–66 loss to Sweden.<ref>{{cite web |title=Georgia 66, Sweden 80 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/national/boxscore/2015-08-13/Georgia-at-Sweden/217916 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=6 February 2019 |date=13 August 2015}}</ref> At the [[2016 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship Division B]], Bitadze averaged 11.4 points, 10.2 rebounds, and 4.1 blocks per game for the [[Georgia national under-19 basketball team|Georgian under-18 team]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Goga Bitadze's profile |url=http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/116061/pid2//sid/12385/tid/2187/tid2//_/2016_FIBA_U18_European_Championship_Division_B/index.html |publisher=[[FIBA]] |accessdate=5 February 2019}}</ref> On 6 August 2016, he recorded tournament-best marks of 23 points and 9 blocks while grabbing 13 rebounds in a 103–101 win over Bulgaria.<ref>{{cite web |title=Georgia 103, Bulgaria 101 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/national/boxscore/2016-08-06/Georgia-at-Bulgaria/239336 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=6 February 2019 |date=6 August 2016}}</ref> Bitadze returned to national team play in 2017, averaging 10.9 points and 6.3 rebounds per game at the [[FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]] Division B.<ref name=realgm/>

=== Senior national team ===
Bitadze was first named to the [[Georgia national basketball team|Georgian senior national team]] at [[EuroBasket 2017]], but a calf ligament injury forced him to sit out of the entire competition. Regardless, he "learned a lot on and off the court" by observing his veteran teammates, including Zaza Pachulia and [[Giorgi Shermadini]].<ref name="facing">{{cite web |title=Facing Raduljica, Zirbes helps Bitadze become big future hope for Georgia |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2019/european-qualifiers/news/facing-raduljica-zirbes-helps-bitadze-become-big-future-hope-for-georgia |publisher=[[FIBA]] |accessdate=6 February 2019 |date=12 January 2018}}</ref> On 24 November 2017, Bitadze debuted for the senior national team versus [[Germany national basketball team|Germany]] during [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Europe)|qualification]] for the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2019 FIBA World Cup]], scoring 4 points in 17 minutes.<ref name=facing/><ref>{{cite web |title=Georgia 70, Germany 79 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/national/boxscore/2017-11-24/Georgia-at-Germany/288805 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=6 February 2019 |date=24 November 2017}}</ref>
